newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien to swear in cabinet next week.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien to swear in cabinet next week.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Wednesday that he planned to swear in his new cabinet in exactly one week.
Chretien's Liberals were re-elected to a second majority government last Monday.
"The new cabinet will be sworn in on Wednesday of next week," Chretien told a news conference.

The old cabinet will meet on Thursday, with a caucus of all Liberal members of Parliament on Monday. After the cabinet was sworn in next Wednesday, the ministers would hold a two-day planning session, he said.
The new parliament will start sitting in September, with a speech from the throne setting out the course of the government.
Chretien would not say who he was eying for future cabinet positions.
"I don't know if there will be any big surprises...but I think I had a good cabinet in the last parliament," the prime minister said.
"It's the second mandate and there will definitely be changes."
Two high-profile cabinet members, Health Minister David Dingwall and Defense Minister Doug Young, lost their seats to low-profile candidates from the left-wing New Democratic Party.

Finance Minister Paul Martin was widely seen returning to his post, although Chretien declined to confirm that on Wednesday. Industry Minister John Manley told Reuters on Wednesday that he hoped to stay in his position too.
